title: Getting started with causalbic
text: bic_fit() fits inflated beta regression (gamlss.dist::BEZI one boundary, gamlss.dist::BEINF two, chosen automatically whether tau.formula supplied). bic_gcomp() estimates average treatment effect decomposes exactly discrete-component part (boundary probability) continuous-component part (conditional mean): conditional effect specific covariate profiles uses decomposition, bic_cate():
code: fit <- bic_fit(y ~ T + W2, nu.formula = ~ T + W1, data = dat) #> GAMLSS-RS iteration 1: Global Deviance = 448.3807  #> GAMLSS-RS iteration 2: Global Deviance = 371.5585  #> GAMLSS-RS iteration 3: Global Deviance = 367.9107  #> GAMLSS-RS iteration 4: Global Deviance = 367.8287  #> GAMLSS-RS iteration 5: Global Deviance = 367.8272  #> GAMLSS-RS iteration 6: Global Deviance = 367.8272 g <- bic_gcomp(fit, treat = "T", data = dat) g #>         tau   tau_alpha      tau_mu  #>  0.06570652 -0.07816620  0.14387272 g["tau_alpha"] + g["tau_mu"] - g["tau"]  # exact identity #> tau_alpha  #>         0 profiles <- data.frame(W1 = c(-1, 0, 1), W2 = c(-1, 0, 1)) bic_cate(fit, "T", profiles) #>          tau   tau_alpha    tau_mu #> 1 0.09744089 -0.05018926 0.1476301 #> 2 0.07395980 -0.07729049 0.1512503 #> 3 0.02791105 -0.11223325 0.1401443

code: cv <- bic_curvature(fit, "T", dat) c(BdT = cv$BdT, discrete = cv$BdT_discrete, continuous = cv$BdT_continuous) #>        BdT   discrete continuous  #> 0.09381095 0.03428841 0.05952254 icim <- bic_icim(cv) sum(icim$influential) #> [1] 63 table(icim$type) #>  #> continuous   discrete  #>        394        206 sens <- bic_sensitivity(cv, fit, "T", dat, tau_hat = g["tau"]) c(L1 = sens$L1, Gamma_star = sens$Gamma_star) #>             L1 Gamma_star.tau  #>       1.028062       1.136554

title: causalbic
text: Causal inference proportional outcomes point mass boundary (zero, one, ), via zero--one inflated beta (BIc) regression Ospina Ferrari (2012). causalbic estimates average conditional treatment effect g-computation decomposes exactly discrete-component contribution (boundary probabilities) continuous-component contribution (conditional mean), consequence block-diagonal Fisher information BIc likelihood. diagnostic layer built separability adds causal conformal normal curvature additive decomposition, per-unit causal influence screen, Hölder-duality sensitivity bound unmeasured confounding. Companion package Ospina (2026), Causal inference proportional outcomes via likelihood displacement inflated beta regression, submitted Annals Applied Statistics. repository package ; include manuscript scripts reproduce simulation application.

text: Companion package Ospina (2026), Causal inference proportional outcomes via likelihood displacement inflated beta regression. Fits zero--one inflated beta (BIc) regression Ospina Ferrari (2012) treatment indicator submodel, estimates average/conditional treatment effect g-computation (bic_gcomp(), bic_cate()), decomposes exactly discrete-component continuous-component contribution, consequence block-diagonal Fisher information BIc likelihood. diagnostic layer built separability adds causal conformal normal curvature additive decomposition (bic_curvature()), per-unit causal influence screen (bic_icim()), Hölder-duality sensitivity bound unmeasured confounding (bic_sensitivity()).
